simple.meaning: חִטָּה (chiṭṭâh) is a Hebrew concept word meaning “wheat , whether the grain or the plant.” BibleIQ follows how Scripture develops this idea across its occurrences.
simple.biblicalBackground: The concept appears 30 times across Genesis, Exodus, Deuteronomy, Judges, Ruth, and 12 more, beginning at Genesis 30:14. Its contexts include family, family line, flock, land.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to חִטָּה (H2406).
simple.whyItMatters: Concept words shape biblical themes. BibleIQ keeps the concept grounded in actual verse evidence instead of starting with a later theological definition.
simple.summary: חִטָּה (chiṭṭâh) / H2406 is traced through Genesis 30:14, Exodus 9:32, Exodus 29:2, Exodus 34:22 as a generated source-based concept entry.

[ חִנְטָה ] noun feminine wheat (see Biblical Hebrew חִטָּה , √ חָנַט ; Nö LCB. Nö 1896 Nö 703 compare Egyptian chnt; Old Aramaic has חטה , plural חטי , Palmyrene חטא Lzb 279 SAC 51 ); — plural חִנְטִין Ezra 6:9 ; 7:22 .
